commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

# Reporting

An ordinary end of turn is not completion. When finished, commit your solution
and send a message with FINAL REPORT on its own line within the first five lines,
followed by these six sections:

FINAL REPORT

The C row is delivered and validated. C could not bind the API before this change. A small, structured resolver refinement closes that gap: the calling file's own `#include <sys/socket.h>` now keys a bare `connect(...)` call on the reviewed header identity `sys/socket.connect`.

## 1. Cause (confirmed with structured evidence)

- **Keying already worked.** #3493 had fixed callable keying, and the two cross-file helper hops (prototype in a header, definition in a `.c` file) already resolved with exhaustive coverage. On the probe tree, the dispatch-outcome query returned `resolved` for both hops and `unknown/open` only for `connect`.
- **The identity was missing.** `resolve_cpp_call` (`get_definition/cpp.rs`) sends `connect` to an include boundary once the workspace has no declaration for it (#3466). The only callee text it kept was the bare name `connect`, which has no owner, so `canonical_external_callee` created no identity.
- **Resulting failures:**
  - Every procedure above the call reported `derivation: incomplete`, `reason: dispatch_unresolved`.
  - The CLI report showed the model active but unused at the same time: `bifrost.web-network-c` selected, `summary_matches: [{symbol: "connect", match_count: 0}]`, run `inconclusive`, exit 2.
- **The #1872 generated header packs do not help.** `CppDependencyPackAdapter` drops every global-namespace free function (`cpp.member_owner_unavailable`), and a C library function is exactly that.

## 2. Changes and reasons

- Base: `18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19`
- Final: `1768aa2e08065c5371808f42d001fcf3fbea3f64`, made of two commits: `f5e06d3b3aaeeb57a1d4fd139dee441a9dbf4189` (the row) and `1768aa2e0…` (open-core inventory rows).

**Include list (`bifrost-cpp` `resolver.rs`).** New `VisibilityIndex::unresolved_includes_visible_before` returns the calling file's tree-sitter include paths that are visible before the call and match no workspace header. It shares one lazy walk with `has_unresolved_include_visible_before`, which still stops at the first match, so the existing hot path costs the same.

**The C proof (`get_definition/cpp.rs`).** New `exact_c_header_function_call`:
- It turns each header into an owner with the existing `module_identity_owner` helper (`sys/socket.h` gives `sys/socket`). That is the same owner an authored summary with a `path` and a bare `symbol` already keys on, so no new string convention is needed.
- It keeps only headers whose active `cpp-c` model declares a function of that name, with no receiver, at the written arity. The arity comes from `call_arity_evidence`, which refuses a count a macro could change.
- It succeeds only if exactly one header survives.
- One name lookup rules out unmodeled names (for example `printf`) before the include walk.

**The route is C only.** C has no overloading and no argument-dependent lookup, so the call can only name the one external function its headers declare. C++ unqualified calls can also reach namespace functions through their arguments' types, which the include set does not decide; that belongs to #3458.

**Proof plumbing (`get_definition/mod.rs`).**
- New constructor `ExactExternalCallProof::c_header_function`.
- The Cpp arm of `resolve_one_with_evidence` now applies the proof.
- JavaScript, Python and Ruby repeated the same five lines to apply their proofs; with C as a fourth user, those lines are now one helper, `record_exact_external_call`.

The change affects only lookups, not stored facts, so no extraction epoch was bumped.

**Row contents.**
- Reviewed model `semantic-packs/web-network/c/bifrost.web-network-c.json` (language `cpp-c`, ecosystem `posix`).
- Shipped policy `bifrost.effects.c.selected-boundary-no-network-io` with an empty selection at ship time; manifest row added and pack version 1.4.0 → 1.5.0.
- Six fixture trees: finding, corrected, recursion, unresolved, `near-miss/workspace-connect`, `near-miss/unrelated-same-name` (a `static` helper in another translation unit).
- Tests, matrix row and section, public docs, CHANGELOG entry.

**Separate findings you may want to file as issues:**
- **(a) Transitive include through a workspace header.** Supporting it would bind the 3 hiredis `net.c` calls; it needs conditional visibility inside the included header.
- **(b) Misleading `workspace-model-inert` warning.** It fires for every external-API workspace model, even when the model binds. I confirmed this on the delivered Rust row. It counts only workspace declarations.
- **(c) Generated header packs drop global C functions.** The #1872 packs drop global-namespace free functions, so real system headers can never supply this route without a reviewed model.

## 6. Draft GitHub approach comment

The C row is ready for review in two commits. C could not bind `connect` before: the resolver kept only the bare name at the include boundary, so the reviewed model was active but matched nothing and every tree was inconclusive. Callable keying from #3493 and the cross-file helper hops already worked. The new route reads the calling file's own unresolved include directives from tree-sitter and turns each header into an owner such as `sys/socket`. A call binds only when exactly one included header's reviewed model declares that function at the written arity. It is limited to C files, because C++ calls can also reach functions through argument types, which is #3458's problem. The finding tree now reports `total -> audit_record -> audit_send -> sys/socket.connect/3` with exhaustive coverage. A workspace `connect` and a same-named `static` helper stay clean, and the unresolved tree stays open. With no model, with the wrong header, or with a different include at the call site, the run reports nothing and does not conclude. On Redis 7.2.4 the two direct POSIX calls in `anet.c` now bind. The three hiredis calls that reach `<sys/socket.h>` through a workspace header stay open, and I suggest a follow-up for transitive includes. No persisted facts changed, so no extraction epoch was bumped.
